# Results — the full measured tables

Everything the README summarises, at full width. Nothing here is typed by hand:
every table is a transcription of a file written by a shipped command.

**The generated files are the source of truth, not this one.** This document is a
convenience copy so a reviewer has one page with all of it. It is *not* checked by
CI — only the block between `<!-- EVAL:BEGIN -->` and `<!-- EVAL:END -->` in
`README.md` is, via `scripts/update_readme.py --check`. If this file and
`eval/reports/` disagree, `eval/reports/` is right and this file is stale.

| table | generated by | lands in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the ablation grid | `make ablate` | [`eval/reports/ablation.md`](../eval/reports/ablation.md) |
| the failure taxonomy | `make taxonomy` | [`eval/reports/failures.md`](../eval/reports/failures.md) |
| judge agreement | `make judge-check` | [`eval/reports/judge.md`](../eval/reports/judge.md) |
| the headline metrics | `make eval` + `make readme` | `eval/reports/<run_id>.json`, README |

Profile for every number below: llm `stub`, embedder `hashing`, judge `heuristic`,
seed 1337. 6 corpus documents, 38 chunks at the shipped chunking, 43 golden cases.

## 1. Ablation — 4 retrieval strategies x 6 chunk configs

`66a15864436b` — the digest of the settings the command was invoked with, the same
one `anchor eval` stamps and the one in the README. (Each cell of the grid is
ingested into a throwaway directory and overrides `chunk_tokens`/`chunk_overlap`, so
a per-cell digest would differ from every other artifact in the repo for reasons
that have nothing to do with the experiment; the two swept fields are printed with

### The report's own verdict, verbatim

> **No strategy beat the BM25 baseline in this run.** The best non-baseline delta
> is -0.045 recall@5 (`hybrid_rerank` at 96/0); every other cell is worse. That is
> the honest result and it is left standing here rather than tuned away.

> **Chunking moved recall@5 by at most 0.045** within a single strategy across the
> 6 configurations.

### Why the grid stops at 144 tokens

`anchor ablate` fingerprints each ingested index (sha256 of its sorted chunk ids)
and prints a banner when two configurations produce the same one, because a
duplicated index is not a second data point. On this corpus that constraint is
binding. The corpus has 38 `##` sections and the longest is **161 tokens**, and
chunking is section-bounded with `min_chunk_tokens: 80`, so every budget at or
above 161 collapses to the same 38-chunk index:

| chunk config | chunks | distinct index? |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 96/0 | 38 | — (the shared index) |
| 96/24 | 43 | yes |
| 96/40 | 44 | yes |
| 112/24 | 44 | yes |
| 128/24 | 43 | yes |
| 144/24 | 39 | yes |
| 256/64 | 38 | no — same index as 96/0 |
| **512/64 (shipped default)** | **38** | **no — same index as 96/0** |
| 1024/128 | 38 | no — same index as 96/0 |

The digests themselves are not transcribed here on purpose: no shipped command
prints them individually, and a hex literal in a document with no command behind it
is the failure mode this repo exists to prevent. The collision is what the tool
reports, and it reports it as a banner — run

```bash
anchor ablate --chunk-configs 96x0,256x64,512x64,1024x128
```

and the generated report opens with `identical index: 96/0, 256/64, 512/64,
1024/128` in place of four data points.

The six grid rows are six distinct indexes. The shipped 512/64 default is
**byte-identical to the grid's 96/0 row**, so the ablation does cover the shipped
configuration — it is just labelled by the smallest budget that produces it.

The consequence is a real limit on the chunking half of this experiment: on a
corpus of 400-word documents there is no resolvable chunking question above 161
tokens. A grid of 256/512/1024 would have produced four identical blocks and the
"chunking barely matters" conclusion would have been a tautology rather than a
finding.

The `entity_substituted` / `unanswerable` group scores 0.000 on every retrieval and
answer metric **by construction** — there is no gold chunk to retrieve and no answer
to match. `abstention_accuracy` is the only column that means anything for it.

`multi_hop` is the weakest answerable slice on every column, and it is also the
slice that is entirely hand-authored (5 cases). Read 0.700 recall@5 there as five
observations, not as a rate.

### The CI floors

`eval/thresholds.yaml`, generated by `make thresholds` from run
`20260914T110919Z-66a15864436b` with `slack: 0.05`. Never hand-edited; `make gate`
fails the build on a breach — five checks.

| bound | metric | value |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| min | `recall_at_5` | 0.8742 |
| min | `recall_at_10` | 0.9348 |
| min | `mrr` | 0.7604 |
| min | `refusal_rate_unanswerable` | 0.65 |
| max | `false_refusal_rate_answerable` | 0.3833 |

Latency and `n_errors` are deliberately not gated: they are machine-dependent, and
a flaky gate is an ignored gate.

Two answer-side metrics are reported in the table above but deliberately **not**
bounded here, both because the bound would have been a second copy of one already
in the list:

* `groundedness`. On the stub profile the generator quotes sentences verbatim out
  of the block it then cites, so every `/v1/query` case scores exactly 0.0 or 1.0
  and the mean is all but `1 - false_refusal_rate_answerable` over the answerable
  slice. The only cases that break the pattern are the 2 agent cases that fold an
  uncited tool value into the answer and score 0.5 — which is why the run's 0.636
  is just short of the 0.667 that identity predicts. `anchor eval` re-checks the
  strict `0.0/1.0` degeneracy on every run and prints a generated note when it
  holds.
* `fabrication_rate_unanswerable`. It counts unanswerable cases that were answered
  **and** cited a document, while `refusal_rate_unanswerable` counts the ones that
  abstained. In this pipeline a non-abstained answer always carries a citation — the
  verifier drops every uncited sentence and builds `citations` only from the markers
  of a supported claim, and the classifier refuses below `partial_ratio` — so over
  that slice fabrication is exactly `1 - refusal_rate_unanswerable` (0.300 against
  0.700 on this run). A ceiling on it was the floor on refusal written twice under
  two names. A provider or grounding path able to emit an uncited answer makes the
  two independent again, at which point it can be gated.

## 3. Failure taxonomy — every case in the worst set

From `eval/reports/failures.md`. The 12 worst cases of the run, ranked by a
deterministic severity key (errored first, then a wrong abstention decision, then
ascending `token_f1`, then ascending recall@5, then case id). Each gets **exactly
one** class, assigned from facts already on the case result — gold chunk ids vs
retrieved vs packed vs the answer — so the assignment is reproducible rather than a
judgement call.

| failure class | n | % of the worst set | what it points at |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `retrieval_miss` | 0 | 0% | the retriever or the chunking: the evidence never came back at all |
| `wrong_chunk_retrieved` | 3 | 25% | ranking, MMR or the context packer: it came back and was dropped |
| `context_ignored_by_generator` | 6 | 50% | the prompt, the extraction rule or the grounding thresholds |
| `genuinely_unanswerable` | 3 | 25% | nothing in the retriever — check the refusal and fabrication rates |

| case | type | class | expected | got | gold retrieved | gold packed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | :-: | :-: |
| `a-0002` | multi_hop | `wrong_chunk_retrieved` | grounded | refused_low_support | yes | no |
| `m-0011` | factual | `wrong_chunk_retrieved` | grounded | refused_no_evidence | yes | no |
| `u-0004` | unanswerable | `genuinely_unanswerable` | refused_no_evidence | grounded | n/a | n/a |
| `u-0008` | unanswerable | `genuinely_unanswerable` | refused_no_evidence | grounded | n/a | n/a |
| `u-0009` | unanswerable | `genuinely_unanswerable` | refused_no_evidence | grounded | n/a | n/a |
| `a-0001` | multi_hop | `context_ignored_by_generator` | grounded | refused_low_support | yes | yes |
| `a-0004` | multi_hop | `context_ignored_by_generator` | grounded | refused_low_support | yes | yes |
| `a-0008` | arithmetic | `context_ignored_by_generator` | grounded | refused_low_support | yes | yes |
| `m-0001` | factual | `context_ignored_by_generator` | grounded | refused_low_support | yes | yes |
| `m-0002` | factual | `context_ignored_by_generator` | grounded | refused_low_support | yes | yes |
| `m-0006` | factual | `context_ignored_by_generator` | grounded | refused_low_support | yes | yes |
| `m-0010` | factual | `wrong_chunk_retrieved` | grounded | refused_no_evidence | yes | no |

Rows are in the report's severity order, not grouped by class.

The generated report carries one fully worked example per class — question, gold
span, top-3 retrieved with text, the packed context with the gold block marked, and
the answer actually produced. Read `eval/reports/failures.md` for those; they are
too long to transcribe here and they are the part worth reading.

**The ordering rule matters and is fixed.** A case the corpus provably cannot answer
is `genuinely_unanswerable` and never `retrieval_miss`, because no correct retrieval
was available to miss. Whether the system fabricated on those cases is reported
separately as `fabrication_rate_unanswerable`.

## 4. Judge validation — full confusion matrix and every disagreement

From `eval/reports/judge.md`, run `2026-09-14T10:50:56Z`. Judge under test:
`heuristic`, the offline default. Scored against 30 frozen `(question, answer,
evidence)` triples in `eval/golden/human_labels.jsonl` — 12 faithful answers, 9 with
one unsupported clause, 9 fabrications. Nothing is retrieved or generated, so this
number does not move when retrieval changes.

| metric | value |
| --- | ---: |
| n | 30 |
| raw agreement | 0.833 |
| Cohen's kappa | 0.749 |

### Confusion matrix (rows = human, columns = judge)

| human \ judge | `grounded` | `partial` | `ungrounded` | recall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `grounded` | 11 | 1 | 0 | 0.917 |
| `partial` | 0 | 9 | 0 | 1.000 |
| `ungrounded` | 0 | 4 | 5 | 0.556 |

### All five disagreements

| id | human | judge | score | what the judge scored | what the human saw |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `hl-0004` | grounded | partial | 0.61 | "A tenant may exceed its daily cap by up to 10%, and traffic inside that band is billed as overage at $0.40 per 1,000 req" | two evidence sentences, both used, nothing added |
| `hl-0022` | ungrounded | partial | 0.50 | "The p95 budget for /v1/rerank is 900 ms and is reviewed annually by the security team." | evidence says 310 ms; both the figure and the reviewer are wrong |
| `hl-0024` | ungrounded | partial | 0.50 | "Starter tier tenants are limited to 1,200 requests per minute and pay a $500 monthly platform fee." | evidence says 600 requests per minute, and Starter is free up to the daily cap |
| `hl-0027` | ungrounded | partial | 0.62 | "A full rebuild of a 10,000 document index takes about 4 hours and runs automatically every night." | evidence says 40 minutes and describes a manual action |
| `hl-0030` | ungrounded | partial | 0.50 | "By December 2025 the gateway p95 had risen to 1,240 ms, breaching the published budget." | evidence says the p95 had settled at 690 ms, inside the budget |

All five disagreements are one class apart, and **four of the five are the same
failure mode**: the judge softened a human `ungrounded` to `partial`. In each of
those four the answer contains a fabricated **number** that contradicts the evidence,
and the lexical judge scores 0.50–0.62 because the surrounding sentence still overlaps
the evidence heavily. The heuristic judge measures lexical support and is blind to
numeric contradiction, so a wrong figure inside an otherwise-copied sentence reads as
half-supported. `ungrounded` recall of 0.556 is the weakest cell in the matrix and
that is exactly where it comes from.

### The judge's labels on real pipeline output

| judge label | cases |
| --- | ---: |
| `grounded` | 25 |
| `partial` | 0 |
| `ungrounded` | 0 |
| `(no verdict — refused)` | 18 |

The judge emitted **one label** across all 43 cases of the golden run. The kappa
above is therefore measured off-distribution: on the hand-written triples the judge
does discriminate, but a classifier that is constant on real output is not
discriminating anything there. `eval/reports/judge.md` prints this distribution on
every run and fires the caveat automatically.

## 5. Refusal behaviour — the threshold sweep

Recomputed from gate features recorded on all 43 cases. No re-run. n=10 unanswerable,
n=33 answerable.

**This curve models the abstain gate only.** 8 of the 18 refusals this run actually
produced came from the gate; the other 10 came from the post-generation low-support
classifier, which is not simulated here. The numbers below are therefore **not** the
system's refusal rates — `refusal_rate_unanswerable` 0.700 and
`false_refusal_rate_answerable` 0.333 in section 2 are.

| gate lexical-overlap threshold | gate-only refusal rate (unanswerable) | gate-only false-refusal rate (answerable) | net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.10 | 0.000 | 0.000 | +0.000 |
| 0.20 | 0.000 | 0.000 | +0.000 |
| 0.30 | 0.300 | 0.061 | +0.239 |
| 0.34  **<- configured gate threshold** | 0.500 | 0.091 | +0.409 |
| 0.40 | 0.500 | 0.182 | +0.318 |
| 0.50 | 0.700 | 0.364 | +0.336 |
| 0.60 | 1.000 | 0.697 | +0.303 |

`net` is refusal minus false-refusal. It is a summary, not an objective: the two
columns trade against each other and which side you want costs less is a product
decision. Because the low-support path is missing from this model, the row where
`net` peaks is **not** a recommendation to move the threshold.

---

## 6. What is not in these tables

* **Latency in anything committed.** Wall clock is machine-dependent. It lives in
  `eval/reports/<run_id>.json` and is compared within one machine's run in
  `eval/reports/ablation.md`, and nowhere else.
* **Any model-quality number.** The default profile is a hashing embedder and an
  extractive stub LLM. These tables measure the pipeline — retrieval, span
  resolution, gating, refusal, citation — not a model.
* **Unanswerability *detection*.** `refusal_rate_unanswerable` measures refusal.
  The control that separates the two was run and it came out flat; see
  [`../eval/golden/PROTOCOL.md`](../eval/golden/PROTOCOL.md), Defence 2.
* **Anything with enough n to be a finding.** 43 cases. One case is 0.023 on a rate,
  and `tool_choice_accuracy` is scored over 4 cases, where one case is 0.250.
